memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"The fire must be kept burning on the altar continuously; it must not go out."'" - Lev 6:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God says it a third time in six verses. The fire must not go out.

When Scripture repeats itself this insistently, it is not padding. It is emphasis. God wanted a permanently burning altar at the centre of His people's life — visible, constant, never needing to be relit.

Practically, this meant that any Israelite, at any hour, could look toward the tabernacle and see smoke rising. Whatever else was uncertain, atonement was always available. The way to God was never closed for the night.

Spiritually, it says something about God's own disposition. He did not want a fire that had to be kindled fresh each time someone needed Him. He wanted one that was always ready.

That is who God still is. Because of Christ, we can approach God's throne of grace with confidence at any moment (Heb 4:16). There is no closing time. No season when He is unavailable. Jesus lives forever to intercede (Heb 7:25) — an unbroken ministry, day and night.

Paul told the Thessalonians never to quench the Spirit's fire (1 Thess 5:19). And to Timothy he wrote, fan into flame the gift of God (2 Tim 1:6).

God's fire is always burning. Ours needs tending.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I live as though God is always available, or as though I must catch Him at the right moment?
2. Is there a flame in my own life that has been allowed to die down?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your welcome never closes. Rekindle in me what has grown cold, and keep me near Your fire. Amen.
